content.text:
I read the disclosure, conversation, and brief first, then traced every claim limitation, numeral, description statement, and figure-brief geometry statement back to affirmative inventor text.

**Ledger result — every item traced:**

- **Claim 1 / 11 (independent):** branch limit below sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor + connector current sensor + control-pilot interface + local connector identifier; upstream branch current sensor; stored authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit; subtract measured non-charging load and configurable safety reserve; sustaining-first then deficit distribution; pilot send + connector verification; reduced pilot command; verification interval then one-at-a-time shedding in stored order — all appear verbatim or near-verbatim in the disclosure.
- **Dependents 2–10, 12–16:** re-measure/stop-when-below (from "one at a time … *until* measured branch current is below"), three reclosure conditions, welded-contactor + inhibit others + local fault indicator, isolated local bus (bus recited only to pilot interfaces and contactors, matching the source enumeration), network interface + nonvolatile token/last accepted limit, outage continuation, token-gated new sessions, tamper-evident meter sequence, and the two-part service-input mapping with agreement-before-store — each has an exact source sentence.
- **Numerals 100–140, 202–216:** each is used with one meaning, each appears in at least one figure brief and in the corresponding description paragraph, and no figure numeral is missing from the ledger. FIG. 4 shape count (seven rectangles + one diamond) matches the eight numbered steps and their stated order.
- **Figure geometry:** the substantive relationships depicted — branch sensor upstream of all three taps, contactor upstream of the connector current sensor (required by "reports zero" and the leakage-threshold test), bus reaching contactor and pilot interface but not the non-charging load, fault indicator external and controller-driven, diamond-vs-rectangle branch and the two non-crossing return paths — all trace to source text. Remaining choices (rectangles, rounded-rectangle vehicle, square/circle sensor symbols, page placement) are shape-neutral schematic conventions confined to the figure briefs; no "by way of example" or "any outline" language leaked into the specification or Brief Description.
- **Definitions checked for smuggled substance:** the energy-deficit, sustaining-current, safety-reserve, leakage-threshold, and shedding-order definitions stay at plain-meaning level and add no undisclosed formula, unit, or value.

No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain, and claims and description use consistent terminology and relationships throughout.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md and the USER passage in input/conversation.md, with input/brief.md used only for formalities (no priority claim, no government support, applicant/inventor Nimo Rotem). I checked and traced the complete set: all 16 claims (independent claims 1 and 11 limitation by limitation, plus every dependent limitation in claims 2-10 and 12-16), all 25 numbered parts in draft/numerals.md (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140 and steps 202-216), all four figure briefs (FIG-1 through FIG-4) including every stated connection, topology, upstream/downstream relationship and flow path, the Brief Description of the Drawings, the Summary, the Detailed Description, and the Abstract. Every limitation traces to an exact affirmative inventor sentence: "whose allowable aggregate current is lower than the sum of the connector ratings"; "Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier"; "A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"; "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus"; "stores, for each active connector, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value"; "subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit"; "first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit"; "sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor"; "opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit" (which also supports the re-measure-and-stop limitation of claims 2 and 12); "A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired"; "A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command"; "inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator"; "stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory"; "does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired"; "Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns"; and "commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the corresponding connector current sensor ... stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector". Substantive drawing relationships are likewise traced: the branch sensor upstream of all connector taps and of the non-charging load follows from "measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"; the connector current sensor downstream of the contactor is required by "its connector current sensor reports zero" and the post-open leakage test; the isolated local bus reaching only the contactors and control-pilot interfaces (and not the non-charging load) matches the source enumeration and claim 5; the external, controller-operated fault indicator matches "operates a local fault indicator". The remaining visual choices (plain rectangles for channels and controller blocks, rounded rectangle for the vehicle, square and circle sensor symbols, block placement on the page, seven rectangles plus one diamond in FIG. 4) are shape-neutral schematic conventions that the briefs label "shown schematically", add no undisclosed proportion, count, material, contact topology or functional-face geometry, and are confined to the figure briefs; no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or similar shape-justifying language appears in the specification or Brief Description. Internal consistency verified: each numeral carries exactly one meaning across text and figures, every figure numeral appears in the ledger and in the corresponding description paragraph, no ledger numeral is orphaned, the FIG. 4 shape count and step order match numerals 202-216 and the described sequence, claim and description terminology and relationships agree (reduced pilot command, verification interval, stored shedding order, three reclosure conditions, welded-contactor inhibit, service-input agreement-before-store), the definitional sentences for energy-deficit value, minimum sustaining current, safety reserve, leakage threshold and shedding order stay at plain-meaning level without smuggling undisclosed formulas or values, no section-line designations are used, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. No unsupported technical assertion or verified inconsistency was found.
